S14.01.needs: a folder open in a trusted workspace, a text file in that folder
S14.01.note: The chooser is VS Code's file dialog opened in the workspace folder, and it accepts text files only (see S14.24), not any device file.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code, and trust the workspace.
Click the + button at the bottom of the message box.
Click Attach workspace files.
In the file dialog, select one text file and click Attach.
Look at the message box: the file name should appear as a chip, ready for the next message.
S14.01.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files

S14.02.needs: a folder open in a trusted workspace, one or more files on the Mac
S14.02.note: The drop target is the composer card (the message box) only, not the whole chat panel.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag one or more text files from Finder onto the message box.
Watch the message box border highlight while the files are over it, then release.
Look at the message box: each dropped file should appear as a chip before sending.
S14.02.where: Drag files from Finder or the VS Code Explorer onto the message box (no visible label)

S14.03.note: Pasted files of any type go through the same intake path; images are sent as image input by the host.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Take a screenshot to the clipboard (Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4), or copy an image.
Click in the message box and press Cmd+V.
Look at the message box: an image chip should appear and the text should not contain the image data.
S14.03.where: Click in the message box and press Cmd+V with an image on the clipboard (no visible label)

S14.08.needs: a Free or paid account is not needed beyond sign-in; an internet connection and a public web page link
S14.08.note: The page is fetched once when attached; the input box title is built as the product name followed by Attach a web page.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Click the + button at the bottom of the message box.
Click Web page.
In the input box, type a full https:// link to a public page and press Enter.
Look at the message box: a chip named after the site's host should appear, or an error that the page could not be read.
S14.08.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Web page, then type the link in the box titled Attach a web page

S14.11.note: No repository attachment was found: the + menu (Attach workspace files, Selection, Open editors, Problems, Git changes, Terminal output, Web page, Browse the web) has no repository item, and the file picker is files-only. Searched apps/extension-vscode for repositor, repo and folder near attach.

S14.12.note: No folder attachment was found: the file picker sets canSelectFolders to false (ChatStateManager.ts), and the + menu has no folder item. Searched apps/extension-vscode for folder near attach.

S14.15.needs: a folder open in a trusted workspace, three or more text files in it
S14.15.note: Picks are capped per batch; a larger selection shows the warning Choose up to N files at a time. The extra files are skipped.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Click the + button, then click Attach workspace files.
In the file dialog, hold Cmd and click three or more text files, then click Attach.
Look at the message box: every selected file should appear as its own chip.
S14.15.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files, then select several files in the dialog and click Attach

S14.16.needs: an image file or an image on the clipboard
S14.16.note: The thumbnail appears only for images added by paste or drag; a picker-added image is refused as binary, so it gets no thumbnail.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Copy an image or take a screenshot to the clipboard.
Click in the message box and press Cmd+V.
Look at the chip: it should show a small picture of the image instead of an icon.
S14.16.where: Paste (Cmd+V) or drag an image (PNG or JPG) into the message box (no visible label)

S14.17.needs: a few sample files of different types
S14.17.note: The icon mapping is in webviewContent.ts; PDF and spreadsheets such as .xlsx use the same chip but the host refuses binary types, so the chip shows a failed note (see S14.24).
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a file with a code extension (for example .ts) onto the message box, then drag a .csv and a .pdf in turn.
Look at each chip's icon: code files show a code icon, csv a table icon, and other types a generic file icon.
S14.17.where: Drag a non-image file onto the message box (no visible label)

S14.18.needs: a text file of known size
S14.18.note: Size appears only on chips added by drag or paste; chips added through Attach workspace files show the name without a size.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a text file of known size onto the message box.
Look at the chip: the file name and a size such as KB or B should show.
Hover over the chip: the tooltip should show the name and size.
S14.18.where: Drag or paste a text file into the message box (no visible label)

S14.22.note: No explicit ready text exists in the code; readiness shows only as the chip losing its faded uploading style and Send becoming enabled.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code, with the message box empty.
Note that the Send button is disabled.
Drag one text file onto the message box.
Wait until the chip stops looking faded, then look at the Send button: it should be enabled.
S14.22.where: Attach any file, then look at the Send button

S14.23.needs: a text file longer than 40,000 characters
S14.23.note: Only the character cut-off is reported; a file that fails to decode shows the warning Some files could not be opened as text. rather than a partial-read notice.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code that has a text file longer than 40,000 characters.
Click the + button, then click Attach workspace files, choose that file and click Attach.
Look at the chip: a Truncated note should appear.
Hover over the chip: the tooltip should say only the first 40,000 characters are sent.
S14.23.where: + button (Attach or use tools) > Attach workspace files, choose a text file longer than 40,000 characters

S14.24.needs: a binary file such as a .zip
S14.24.note: Through Attach workspace files the refusal instead appears as a VS Code warning Choose text files for workspace context., not as a chip.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a .zip file onto the message box.
Look at the chip: the file name should be followed by the reason in brackets.
S14.24.where: Drag a binary file (for example a .zip) onto the message box

S14.28.note: The × button's accessible name is Remove attachment followed by the file name.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a text file onto the message box, or use + > Attach workspace files.
Click the × on the chip; the chip should disappear and Send should disable if the box is empty.
Type a question that asks what the file contains and send it; the reply should not use the removed file's content.
S14.28.where: Attach a text file, then click the × on its chip

S14.32.needs: a binary file such as a .zip and a text file
S14.32.note: Per-file errors show on drag or paste chips; the file picker instead joins its skip reasons into one VS Code warning.
steps: Sign in and open a folder in VS Code.
Drag a .zip file onto the message box.
Look at that file's chip: its name should be followed by the reason, not a generic message.
Drag a valid text file in the same drop and check that its chip shows no error.
S14.32.where: Drag a file the chat refuses (for example a .zip) onto the message box
